$comment: How old a reading is, and when a window refills, in the words every Quota client uses. One rule, one voice: the menu bar footer, a provider row, a device row, the website, and the widgets all state age relative to now rather than as a clock time or a calendar date, because an absolute instant makes the reader do the subtraction. `age` is the bare relative phrase; `observation` is the whole line under a reading, which names why a reading is not current instead of only that it is not; `device` is the age half of a device row; `missing_reset` is whether a percent window with no refill instant prints the no-reset phrase; `reset` is the line under a window that still has a future refill. Weekday and month cases pin `now` and `resets_at` as RFC 3339 with an offset so every runtime formats that local time. `packages/apple-shared` and `apps/web/src/lib/format.ts` both answer this file, so a phrase one of them changes cannot drift from the other.

age.name: under a minute reads as an instant, not a ticking second count
the last second before a minute is still an instant
a whole minute is the first age worth a number
minutes run to the last one before an hour
hours run to the last one before a day
days run to the last one before a week
weeks run to the last one before a year
a reading stamped in the future is not negative

observation.name: a current reading says when it was taken
a current reading hours old still says so plainly
a reading that aged out says it is not current
a source that lost its sign-in names that instead
a source that could not be reached names that instead
a source that cannot answer at all names that instead
a source that failed names that instead

missing_reset.name: a full percent window omits the phrase
a used percent window with no refill uses the phrase
a balance-only window never uses the phrase

device.name: a device that reported a week ago
a device the Account has never heard from

reset.name: the last second before a minute still rounds up to a minute
a whole minute is the first exact minute
the last second before an hour rounds up into the hour
an hour drops the zero minutes
three hours exactly omits the minutes
three hours and twelve minutes names both
the last minute before a day still counts in hours
a day away names the weekday and the 24-hour local time
the last hour before a week still names the weekday
a week away names the month and day
a reset that has already passed prints nothing
a reset a day ago prints nothing
